# Function timing catalogue

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask bench-functions` from crates/engine/examples/bench_functions.rs. Don't edit by hand. -->

> **Generated** for Cella 0.13.0 at `b4f2870` (2026-11-24). Machine: windows x86_64. Each number is the fastest of 5 passes. Method and what a row does not measure: [performance.md](performance.md).

**One row per registered worksheet function.** The command catalogue prices the command surface and the scenario gate prices the operations a session spends its seconds on; this prices the formulas inside the cells — a user's spreadsheet is mostly functions, and before this page not one of them had a number.

A cell is the wall clock of `cell.set` with that formula: parse it, evaluate it, write the cell. `small` gives every range argument ten rows; `whole` gives it the whole column (the workbook's data is a header and `rows − 1` rows of eight columns). `scalar` means the call has no range argument, so the same call is both scales. A template's `$R`, `$T` … stands for one of those ranges; the exact calls are in [../xtask/bench-functions.txt](../xtask/bench-functions.txt).

A note reads `error by design` for a function whose documented answer is an error here (a CUBE function with no connection, `NA`), `error` for a call the engine answered with a `#` error, and `refused` when the formula would not go in at all. Otherwise the note is the line's own words in [../xtask/bench-functions.txt](../xtask/bench-functions.txt), for a call that is not what the sheet's shape suggests: a FORECAST.ETS series stops at the engine's 200,000-point cap, and a transpose or TOROW cannot take a whole column because the result would pass the 16,384-column limit.

**The floor.** Entering a formula that does nothing (`=1+1`) costs 170 us ms at 100,000 rows and 976 us ms at 1,000,000 rows — that is the session taking its undo snapshot and the recalculation bookkeeping, not the function. Every scalar row is mostly this floor: read a scalar number as "the floor, plus whatever the function itself added".
